gaps.sentence: You ___ touch that wire — it carries a live current!
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' signals something absolutely not allowed: mustn't touch.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ leave the examination room without permission.
gaps.explanation: Formal rules use 'may not' (or 'must not') to deny permission: may not leave.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather not comment until the investigation is over.
gaps.hint: a polite refusal with would rather not
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather not' declines politely: would rather not.

gaps.sentence: It ___ be the postman — he has already been this morning.
gaps.hint: ruled out by what already happened
gaps.explanation: Evidence that rules something out uses 'can't': can't be.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: You really ___ to apologise before this gets worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses advice similar to 'should': ought to apologise.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have brought a present, but it was kind of her anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' plus the participle means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have brought.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.
